questions.question: In story S13 (Leave with eligibility, local purge (abandon) and disband surfacing), is there any vacuous or placeholder production path: a no-op/stub body, a tautological assertion, a frozen stand-in constant, or an optional dependency (injected port, handler, client handle) that silently degrades to non-behavior when not injected? Cite file:line for each injection point in app/src/lib/marmot/membership/index.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/membership/leaveEligibility.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/membership/leaveGroup.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/membership/purgeLocalGroup.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/membership/groupNotifications.ts; app/tests/unit/marmot/membership/*.test.ts and show that omitting the dependency fails loudly rather than succeeding silently.

Could `membership` be deleted and rewritten without modifying any file outside its `dependencies_allowed` list? If not, which cross-module dependencies exist and do they flow through declared seam contracts in architecture.md (imports only via each module's index.ts, no React-context imports under app/src/lib/marmot/**, no ts-mls or @internet-privacy/marmot-ts imports)?

Does S13 comply with the architecture.md boundary rules: only `client/` constructs or disposes the MarmotClient, code inside HistoryBackend calls / inbox handlers / client listeners never awaits an account-scope client call (follow-up work via the owned setTimeout(0) FIFO), group sender identity comes only from orderingKey.account, and idb-keyval update() is not used? List each rule touched by this story's files with file:line evidence, or state why it is not touched.

Do unit, property, and (where the AC names them) library-harness or e2e tests cover the artifacts named in S13's scope (app/src/lib/marmot/membership/index.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/membership/leaveEligibility.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/membership/leaveGroup.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/membership/purgeLocalGroup.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/membership/groupNotifications.ts; app/tests/unit/marmot/membership/*.test.ts)? Show that tests use real collaborators or test fixtures rather than mocking the helper used at the SUT call site, that idb mocks are seeded out of key order where order matters, and that at least one test fails if the production code is replaced by a no-op.

Does the delivered S13 implementation match the intent of its scope (membership/: pure leave eligibility with twin-read discipline on library accessors, immediate UI removal + background group.leave() with kind-9 left announcement (bounded, soft-fail), failure restore with leave-failed toast, no durable leaving marker; purgeLocalGroup (group.abandon + overlay/member ) and respect its exclusions (Deleting old leave impls/tombstones (S22); e2e leave rewrites (S25))? Identify any capability owned by a later story that was built ahead, or any in-scope capability left unimplemented.

Which trust or validation boundaries does S13 touch (signer budget/permissions, relay-supplied events, rumor sender/pubkey attribution, invite/join payloads, privacy invariant that no profile metadata is published to public relays)? Show the validation or defensive check at each boundary with file:line evidence and a test that feeds a malformed or hostile input and observes rejection.

Seam contract GroupDataPurger (consumed beyond S13; consumers: S17): does the delivered artifact at app/src/lib/marmot/membership/purgeLocalGroup.ts expose exactly the declared shape (fields: purgeLocalGroup: (groupId: string) => Promise<void>) and uphold each invariant (calls group.abandon() and removes overlay, member profiles, chat/poll rows, history rows, invite links, markers; idempotent on second call)? Show the type/definition with file:line and a test asserting each invariant, including enum/constant membership and value ranges where the contract constrains them.

AC-LEAVE-1: Eligibility (app-side, pure function): sole member → `abandon` (no `leave()` call, local purge only); sole admin with other members → blocked with the last-admin outcome and no `leave()` call; otherwise → `leave`. Truth table asserted over {members:1,2+} × {isAdmin} × {otherAdmins 0,1+}. The twin-read discipline (leaveGroupImpl and live-member read both guarded against a corrupt-state throw, with opposite fail-closed directions) MUST be kept: a throwing `members()` accessor MUST NOT skip the purge on the leave path and MUST fail closed on the live-member path. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-LEAVE-2: On leave, the group MUST disappear from the app group list immediately (before `leave()` settles); `leave()` MUST run in the background; the library group MUST be gone from `groups.list()` within 15 s (harness with real timing options); kind-9 "left" announcement MUST be sent first with a bounded wait and MUST soft-fail (a rejecting/hanging announcement does not block `leave()`). Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit + harness] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-LEAVE-3: If `leave()` rejects or times out (other than `last-admin`), the group MUST be restored to the list and the existing leave-failed toast i18n key MUST be shown. No durable "leaving" marker MUST be written (idb/localStorage scan after a mid-leave reload shows none; the group is listed again). Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit; e2e:groups-leave-intent (rewritten)] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-MEM-4: On `groupRemoved`, and at startup for any listed group whose `members()` lacks the own account (since `groupRemoved` is at-most-once), the app MUST run the local purge: library `group.abandon()` plus removal of app-side group data (overlay, member profiles, chat and poll rows, history rows via `purge`, invite links, markers), then update the UI so the group is gone. Tests: (a) event path; (b) startup-check path with no event; (c) second call is idempotent. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit + harness; e2e:groups-remove-member (kept)] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-MEM-5: Disbanded/fenced groups MUST be surfaced through the existing UI state derived from `onNotification`; a disband notification marks the group disbanded in the overlay. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.
